titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§93–99: The Sable Coat and the Dawn Alarm
part: §§93–99 — The Sable Coat and the Dawn Alarm
about: Seven sections, from a homecoming to an alarm. In §93 Naqu-Bayan weeps for his lost son Bo'orchu, who comes home, then sends him off with Temüjin, who in turn goes back to his own family at the Senggur stream. §94 goes back to De-Sechen, who gives Börte-Üjin to Temüjin as wife and sends her with her mother Sotan. §95 is Bo'orchu's leaving his father's house to keep company with Temüjin. In §96 the family moves to Burgi on the upper Kerülen and Temüjin carries Sotan's gift of a black sable coat to Wang Qan, who promises to gather his scattered people. In §97 the old man Jarchiudai gives his son Jelme to Temüjin. §98 is the dawn alarm, Qo'aqchin's cry that the earth is shaking; §99 is the family's flight on horseback, with the shortage of one horse. The grammar to watch is the converb chain (-žu / -žü / -ču / -ġed, Ming 着, 'having ...-ing'), the quotation frame (ügülerün 'saying' opening and keġen / keġebe closing a speech), the reflexive-possessive (-ben / -jen / -jan, 'one's own'), the reciprocal -ldü- ('one another'), and the participle -gsen with the instrumental -ġer, 'because of having ...'. The hard places, flagged in the notes, are who is nine years old in §94, the meaning of the words for 'kidney's point' in §96, the dawn phrase and the žalγamsiγtan line in §98, and the identity of the unit's quiet subjects.

sentences.t: Naqu-Bajan-(n)u ger-tür kürbe.
sentences.l: Naqu-Bajan's home-at, reached.
sentences.i: He reached Naqu-Bayan's home.
sentences.n: The subject is Bo'orchu, but the Mongol line does not say so; it is carried over from the end of §92 and from the next sentence, which names the father. ger-tür is ger 'home' plus the dative-locative -tür, Ming 家裏 'in the home'; kürbe (到了) is kür- 'reach' plus the past -ba, which becomes -be after front vowels. This part is cut into many short units because its sentences chain many converbs (-žu, -žü, -ču, Ming 着); I have broken each chain at the natural clause and said so where it matters.

morph.gloss: Naqu Bayan, Bo'orchu's father (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: Naqu-Bajan köġü-ben Boγ̇orču-ji žaγažu nisun nilbusu-bar ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Naqu-Bajan, son-his-own, Boγ̇orču (acc.), having-lost, tears, tear-with, was.
sentences.i: Naqu-Bayan, who had lost his son Bo'orchu, had been in tears.
sentences.n: Ming 失着 'having lost / missed' glosses žaγažu, with the converb -žu; I cannot name the stem (žaγa-) with confidence. Boγ̇orču-ji is the name plus the accusative -ji (Ming 行), 'Bo'orchu as object'. köġü-ben is köġü 'son' plus the reflexive-possessive -ben, Ming 自的 'one's own'. nisun nilbusu-bar: nisun is Ming 涕 and nilbusu-bar is nilbusu 'tear' (淚) with the instrumental -bar, where the Ming adds 敎 ('cause'); I take the pair as a doubled 'tears' phrase, 'in tears'. ažuγ̇u (有來) is a- 'be' with a past ending, 'was'. The full stop is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: Naqu Bayan, Bo'orchu's father (personal name) [人名]
son (short form of köġün) [兒子 (自的)行]
Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名行]
accusative after a vowel: marks the object
to lose, miss (stem inferred from the Ming) [失着]
instrumental: with, by (the Ming adds 敎 'cause'; uncertain)

sentences.t: Genedte kürtežü köġü-ben üžežü nigente uilamu; nigente doṅγodumu.
sentences.l: Suddenly, having-reached, son-his-own having-seen, once weeps; once marvels.
sentences.i: When his son suddenly arrived and he saw him, at one moment he wept, and at the next he marvelled.
sentences.n: A converb chain of three (kürtežü, üžežü, then the two finite verbs). nigente nigente is Ming 一次 一次, 'one time ... another time', the 'now ... now' pattern; nigen 'one' with the dative-locative -te. uilamu (哭有) and doṅγodumu (怪有) are present-tense verbs in -mu, Ming 有 'is (doing)'. Neither stem is certain: uila- 'weep' is clear from the Ming, doṅγodu- 'marvel' is inferred from 怪 'think strange'. Shiratori's semicolon divides the two halves.

morph.gloss: to arrive, come to (from kür- 'reach'; uncertain) [到着]
son (short form of köġün) [兒 自的行]
to marvel, think strange (stem inferred from the Ming) [怪有]

sentences.t: Köġün in-ü Boγ̇orču ügülerün:
sentences.l: Son, his, Boγ̇orču, saying:
sentences.i: His son Bo'orchu said:
sentences.n: Köġün in-ü is 'son, his': the third-person genitive in-ü follows its noun (Ming 他的), a pattern the text uses for 'his son'. ügülerün (說) is ügüle- 'speak' plus the converb -rün and opens a quotation, as it will every time in this part; the quotation's opening mark is at the next word.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: "Jaγ̇un bolba.
sentences.l: "What has-become.
sentences.i: "What is the matter?
sentences.n: Doubtful. Ming gives 甚麽 做了, 'what has been made / has become'. I take it as Bo'orchu's question about his father's tears; it could also be an exclamation, 'what a thing!'. bolba is bol- 'become' plus the past -ba.

sentences.t: Sain nökör muṅtanižu aisun ažuγ̇u; nököčežü odulaγ̇a bi.
sentences.l: Good companion, hardship-ing, come was; companion-being, gone-I.
sentences.i: A good companion came to me in hardship, and I went off as his companion.
sentences.n: Hard to pin down. Ming 好伴當 艱難 來有來 做伴着 去了來 我. The 'good companion' is Temüjin, whom Bo'orchu has gone with; the Mongol never names him, and the English supplies 'to me'. muṅtanižu is a converb from a stem muṅtana- 'be in hardship' that the known-forms gloss infers from the Ming; aisun is aisu- 'come' with an ending (-n) I cannot classify. ažuγ̇u and odulaγ̇a are both past narrative forms ('was', 'went'). Shiratori's full stop after bi and his semicolon after ažuγ̇u mark the sentence ends.

morph.gloss: to be in hardship (stem inferred from the Ming) [(艱)難︀]
to be a companion (from nökör) [做伴着]
past narrative: went (linking vowel plus -laγ̇a; uncertain)

sentences.t: Edöġe irebe" kēġed
sentences.l: Now come-I," having-said,
sentences.i: Now I have come," he said, and
sentences.n: irebe (來了) is ire- 'come' plus the past -be, and the quotation closes on it. The speaker is Bo'orchu; the Mongol has no 'I' here, the subject being in the verb context. kēġed is keġe- 'say' plus the converb -ġed, run together and written long (Ming 說了, 'having said'); it hands the sentence on to the next action.

sentences.t: qaγ̇ulžu odču keġer-e buγuγsan nambuγa saγ̇uluγa-ban abčiraba.
sentences.l: Galloping, going, in-the-steppe having-covered skin-bucket, skin-pail-his-own, brought.
sentences.i: He galloped off and brought back the leather bucket that he had covered over in the open country, and his own leather pail.
sentences.n: A converb pair (qaγ̇ulžu odču: 'galloping, going') leads to one finite verb, abčiraba, 'brought'. Ming 葢了的 for buγuγsan is 'covered', and I read it as a participle (-γsan) qualifying nambuγa; whether 'covered over', 'hidden' or 'buried' is not certain, and the stem buγu- is my inference. keġer-e is keġer 'steppe, open ground' with the dative-locative -e. saγ̇uluγa-ban is 'pail' with the reflexive-possessive -ban, 'his own'. The English 'covered over' is the cautious choice.

morph.gloss: converb: having ...-ed, ...-ing (after r or a vowel)
to cover over (stem inferred from the Ming; uncertain) [葢了的]
skin pail, milk-pail [皮斗 自的行]
to bring along (ab- 'take' plus a second verb; uncertain) [將來了]

sentences.t: Temüžin-(n)e tel-quriγan alažu künesü ögüġed
sentences.l: To-Temüžin, suckling-lamb having-killed, provisions having-given,
sentences.i: He killed a lamb that had been feeding on two mothers' milk and gave Temüjin provisions for the road,
sentences.n: tel-quriγan is Ming 喫二母乳的羔兒 'a lamb that has drunk the milk of two mothers', a fat lamb; the compound is analysed from the Ming and is uncertain. künesü (行糧) is food for a journey. Temüžin-(n)e is the name with the dative -(n)e (Ming 行), 'to Temüjin'; the (n) is Shiratori's. ögüġed is ög- 'give' plus the converb -ġed with a linking vowel (Ming 與了). The sentence is a converb chain that I have broken here and at the next unit.

morph.gloss: lamb that has fed on two mothers' milk (compound; analysis from the Ming, uncertain) [喫二 母乳的羔兒]

sentences.t: nambuγa deġürge žasažu künesüleġülbe.
sentences.l: Skin-bucket, load, having-prepared, provisions-made-to-be-made.
sentences.i: He had the leather bucket made ready as a load, and had provisions prepared.
sentences.n: deġürge (駄的) is 'loaded, a pack load', from deġür- 'carry on the back of a beast'. žasažu is žasa- 'prepare' plus the converb -žu. künesüleġülbe is künesü 'provisions' plus -le- (making a verb) plus the causative -ġül- plus the past -be; Ming 行糧敎做了, 'caused provisions to be made', i.e. had them prepared. Nobody is named as the doer in this line.

morph.gloss: load, pack (from deġür- 'to load, carry') [駄的]
to prepare, set in order [整治着]
provisions for a journey [行糧敎做了]
makes a verb: to make into

sentences.t: Naqu-Bajan ügülerün:
sentences.l: Naqu-Bajan, saying:
sentences.i: Naqu-Bayan said:
sentences.n: The usual speech-opener: ügülerün, 'saying'.

morph.gloss: Naqu Bayan, Bo'orchu's father (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: "Qojar žalaγ̇us bi.
sentences.l: "Two young-men are.
sentences.i: "You are two young men.
sentences.n: Ming 兩箇 少年每 有. The Mongol has no pronoun; the 'you' is from the Ming 您 (ta) at the next word, which belongs to the following clause. žalaγ̇us is žalaγ̇u 'youth' plus the plural -s (少年每). bi here is the verb 'is, are' (Ming 有), not the pronoun bi 'I'; the two homographs are a real hazard in this text.

morph.gloss: is, are (verb; possibly a short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.t: Ta üželdügtüd mönö qoina bu tebčildügtüd" keġebe
sentences.l: You look-after-one-another; from-tomorrow after, do-not forsake-one-another," said.
sentences.i: Look after one another; from now on, never abandon one another," he said.
sentences.n: Two imperatives with the reciprocal -ldü- 'one another' (Ming 相) and a plural-polite ending -gtüd (Ming 您 'you'), spelled -tüd here: üželdügtüd from üže- 'see, look to', tebčildügtüd from tebči- 'leave, abandon' (the stem is guessed from the Ming 棄). bu (休) is the prohibitive 'do not'. mönö qoina is Ming 明 後, 'tomorrow, after', i.e. 'from now on' or 'henceforth'; I give the second sense. keġebe (說了) closes the quotation: keġe- 'say' plus -be.

morph.gloss: imperative, second person plural: do ye ...!
tomorrow (Ming 明; with qoina, 'from now on') [明]
to forsake, abandon (stem inferred from the Ming) [相棄您]
imperative, second person plural: do ye ...!

sentences.t: Temüžin odču γurban süni γurban üdür jorčižu Seṅgür γoroqan-a ger-tür(i)-jen kürbe.
sentences.l: Temüžin, going, three nights, three days, travelling, Seṅgür stream-at, home-at-his-own, reached.
sentences.i: Temüjin set out, travelled three nights and three days, and reached his own home on the Senggur stream.
sentences.n: One converb chain (odču ... jorčižu) to one finite verb. γurban süni γurban üdür is 'three nights, three days'. γoroqan-a is γoroqan 'small river' with the dative-locative -a. ger-tür(i)-jen is ger 'home' + -tür (dative-locative) + the reflexive-possessive -(i)jen 'one's own', the bracketed i being Shiratori's; the Ming has 家裏 自的行 'at one's own home'.

morph.gloss: converb: having ...-ed, ...-ing (after r or a vowel)
to go, set out, travel [去着]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the bracketed i is Shiratori's)

sentences.t: Höġelün eke, Qasar kiġed deġü-ner in-ü herüžü ažu üžežü bajasba.
sentences.l: Höġelün the mother, Qasar and younger-brothers, his, worrying, staying, having-seen, rejoiced.
sentences.i: His mother Hö'elün, Qasar and his younger brothers, who had been anxious about him, were glad when they saw him.
sentences.n: Another converb chain (herüžü ažu üžežü) to one finite verb, bajasba, 'rejoiced' (喜歡了). herüžü is Ming 愁着 'grieving, being anxious'; the stem herü- is inferred. ažu is a- 'be' as a converb, and with herüžü it makes 'had been worrying'. kiġed (等) is 'and' or 'and the like'; deġü-ner is deġü 'younger brother' with the plural -ner. in-ü, 'his', stands after deġü-ner but belongs to the whole group.

morph.gloss: Hö'elün, a woman's name (personal name) [母名]
Qasar, a son's name (personal name) [人名]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to grieve, be anxious (stem inferred from the Ming) [愁着]

sentences.t: Tendēče Temüžin Belgütei qojar De-Sečen-(n)ü Börte-Üžin-i jesün nasutu büküi-dür üžežü
sentences.l: From-there Temüžin, Belgütei, two, De-Sečen's Börte-Üžin (acc.), nine aged, being-when, having-seen,
sentences.i: From there, Temüjin and Belgütei, who had seen De-Sechen's Börte-Üjin when she was nine years old,
sentences.n: A backward-looking clause and a real doubt. Ming 九歲(有的) 有時 gives 'when being nine years old' (jesün nasutu büküi-dür), but the Mongol does not say whose age it is. I put it on Börte, as the nearest noun; it could be Temüjin's, since the meeting at De-Sechen's goes back to their boyhood. Tendēče is tende 'there' plus the ablative -ēče. nasutu is nasu 'age' + the possessive -tu, 'having years'. Börte-Üžin-i is the name plus the accusative -i. The English leaves the doubt open with 'she was'.

morph.gloss: ablative: from (long vowel from tende plus -eče)
Belgütei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
De-Sechen, a man's name (personal name) [人名 的]
Börte-Üjin, a woman's name (personal name) [人名 行]

sentences.t: iregseġer qaγačažu büleġe.
sentences.l: having-come-because, having-parted, had-been.
sentences.i: had come away from her, and had been apart.
sentences.n: Another stage of the same sentence. iregseġer is ire- 'come' + the participle -gsen + the instrumental -ġer, 'on account of having come' (the known-forms gloss, Ming 說來的上頭). qaγačažu is qaγača- 'part from' plus -žu. büleġe is bü- 'be' plus the past -leġe (Ming 來 'used to'). I read the three as one idea: they had parted and long been apart.

morph.gloss: to part from, separate from [離着]

sentences.t: Kelüren müren huruγ̇u erin odba.
sentences.l: Kelüren river, along, seeking, went.
sentences.i: They went looking along the Kerülen river.
sentences.n: huruγ̇u (順) is 'along, downstream'. erin is eri- 'seek' plus the converb -n. The subject, Temüjin and Belgütei, is carried from the sentence before. Shiratori writes the river Kelüren.

morph.gloss: the Kerülen, a river name [河名]

sentences.t: Čegčer Čiγurγu qojar-un žaγ̇ura De-Sečen Uṅgirad tende ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Čegčer, Čiγurγu, two's between, De-Sečen, Uṅgirad, there was.
sentences.i: Between the two mountains Chegcher and Chigurgu, De-Sechen of the Ungirad people was living.
sentences.n: Ming 山名 山名 兩箇的 路間 人名 姓氏 那裏 有來. qojar-un žaγ̇ura is 'between the two' (the genitive -un with žaγ̇ura 'midway'). Uṅgirad is Ming 姓氏, a clan name, which I give as 'the Ungirad'. The English 'was living' is my gloss on ažuγ̇u 'was', the sense required by 'there was'.

morph.gloss: De-Sechen, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
the Ungirad, a people or clan name [姓氏]

sentences.t: De-Sečen Temüžin-i üžežü maši jeke bajasču ügülerün:
sentences.l: De-Sečen, Temüžin (acc.), having-seen, very greatly rejoicing, saying:
sentences.i: De-Sechen saw Temüjin and, greatly rejoicing, said:
sentences.n: A short chain: üžežü, bajasču, then ügülerün, which opens the speech that follows. maši jeke is Ming 好生 大, an intensifying pair, 'very greatly'.

morph.gloss: De-Sechen, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
converb: having ...-ed, ...-ing (after r or a vowel)

sentences.t: "Taičiγ̇ud aqa deġü čin-u naitamu keġen medežü maši herüžü čüköleġei.
sentences.l: "Taičiγ̇ud brothers, you-of, envy, saying, having-known, very worrying, I-despaired.
sentences.i: "I knew that the Taichi'ud brothers were jealous of you, and I was very anxious and had lost hope.
sentences.n: Ming 姓氏 兄 弟 你的 嫉妒 麽道 知着 好生 愁着 絕望. aqa deġü is 'elder and younger brother', i.e. 'the brothers'. čin-u is či 'you' with the genitive -u. keġen medežü is 'saying (so), knowing', the quotation marker keġen followed by the verb; I take it as 'knowing that they envy you'. The last word, čüköleġei, has no tense marker I can name; the ending -ġei could be an optative or a present, and the stem čüköle- is inferred from 絕望 'give up hope'. I render it 'had lost hope'; that is a guess at the tense.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people or clan name [姓氏]
you (stem čin- before case endings) [你的]
to envy, be jealous (stem inferred from the Ming) [嫉妒]
converb that closes a quotation: saying
to grieve, be anxious (stem inferred from the Ming) [愁着]
to lose hope, despair (stem inferred from the Ming) [絕望]

sentences.t: Aran užebe že čima-ji"
sentences.l: Hardly I-saw indeed you (acc.)"
sentences.i: "I have scarcely seen you!"
sentences.n: Ming 僅得 見了 也者 你行. aran is 'barely, only just'; užebe is üže- 'see' plus the past -be, spelled with u here; že is the particle of emphasis (Ming 也者); čima-ji is či 'you' in its oblique stem čima- with the accusative -ji. The line is an exclamation: it was a near thing to see him again.

morph.gloss: accusative after a vowel: marks the object

sentences.t: kēġed Börte-Üžin-i neileġüleġed eġüsgebe.
sentences.l: having-said, Börte-Üžin (acc.), having-caused-to-join, sent-off.
sentences.i: Having said so, he joined Börte-Üjin to him and sent her away with him.
sentences.n: neileġüleġed is neile- 'join' (Ming 相配 'be matched') + the causative -ġül- + -ġed, 'having caused to be joined', which I read as 'gave in marriage'. eġüsgebe (送將去了) is 'sent off, saw off'; the stem eġüsge- is inferred. The next unit begins with the same word as a converb. I do not know the exact marriage law here; the English follows the Ming.

morph.gloss: Börte-Üjin, a woman's name (personal name) [人名 行]
to join, unite (Ming 相配 'match') [相配了]
to send off, see off (stem inferred from the Ming) [送將去了]

sentences.t: Eġüsgen aisurun. De-Sečen žaγ̇ura Kerülen-ü Uraγčul-nu-dāča qariba.
sentences.l: Seeing-off, when-coming, De-Sečen on-the-way, Kelüren's Uraγčul's corner-from, turned-back.
sentences.i: He escorted them, and as they came, De-Sechen turned back on the road at the corner of Uraqchul on the Kerülen.
sentences.n: Eġüsgen (迭) is the same stem eġüsge- as converb, 'seeing off'; the Ming gloss 迭 ('in turn, repeatedly') is odd and I take it as 'escorting'. aisurun (來時) is 'when coming'. Uraγčul-nu-dāča is Uraγčul (place) + the genitive -nu + a long -dāča, Ming 隅自 'from the corner'; the word for 'corner' and the form of the ending are uncertain. qariba (囘了) is qari- 'return' + -ba. The meaning that De-Sechen went back part way, leaving the party, is clear from the Ming.

morph.gloss: to send off, see off (stem inferred from the Ming) [迭]
De-Sechen, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
the Kerülen, a river name [河名 的]
Uraqchul, a place name [地名 的 隅自]
ablative: from (Ming 隅自 'from the corner'; analysis uncertain)

sentences.t: Gergei in-ü Börte-Üžin-ü eke Sotan neretei büliġi.
sentences.l: Wife, his, Börte-Üžin's mother, Sotan named, was.
sentences.i: His wife, Börte-Üjin's mother, was named Sotan.
sentences.n: gergei (妻) is 'wife'; in-ü, 'his', refers to De-Sechen. neretei is nere 'name' + the possessive -tei, 'having the name' (named). The Ming 有來 for büliġi is the same as for büleġe; the tense is a past, 'had been', and the English keeps a simple past.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
Börte-Üjin, a woman's name (personal name) [妻名 的]
Sotan, a woman's name (personal name) [母名]

sentences.t: Sotan öki-jen hüdežü Kürelkü dotora Seṅgür γoroqan-a büküi-dür kürgežü irebe.
sentences.l: Sotan, daughter-her-own having-escorted, Kürelkü inside, Seṅgür stream-at being-when, having-brought-to, came.
sentences.i: Sotan escorted her own daughter, brought her to the Senggur stream inside the Kürelkü mountains, and came.
sentences.n: Converb chain (hüdežü ... kürgežü) to one finite verb, irebe. hüdežü is hüde- 'see off, escort' (the bride sense is from context), and kürgežü is kür- 'reach' made causative (Ming 送到, 'send to the end'). Ming gives 山名 for Kürelkü; I treat it as a mountain or range, 'inside' it (dotora). büküi-dür is 'when being', here 'when at'. The two verbs with 'came' and 'brought' show the mother travelling with the bride all the way.

morph.gloss: Sotan, a woman's name (personal name) [(母)名]
to bring to, deliver (kür- 'reach' made causative; uncertain) [送到着]

sentences.t: Sotan-(n)i qariγuluγ̇ad Belgütei-ji Boγ̇orču-ji "nököčeje" keġen urižu irebe.
sentences.l: Sotan (acc.), having-sent-back, Belgütei (acc.), Boγ̇orču (acc.), "let-us-be-companions", saying, having-called, came.
sentences.i: He sent Sotan back, then called Belgütei and Bo'orchu, saying "Let us be companions," and they came.
sentences.n: Two doubts. First, the subject of the whole chain is not written, but the Ming (敎囘了 'caused to return') shows that someone sent Sotan back, and I read this as Temüjin. Second, irebe is glossed 去了 'went' by the Ming, but ire- means 'come'; I give 'came' (the two called came to him). nököčeje is nököče- 'be a companion' plus -je, the first-person plural hortative 'let us' (Ming 咱 'we'). qariγuluγ̇ad is qari- 'return' + the causative -γul- + -γ̇ad.

sentences.i: Bo'orchu brought Belgütei to his own father, and without a word to him,
sentences.n: kürġeġülüġed is kür- 'reach' with a causative (敎到了), 'caused to arrive', hence 'brought'. ečige-dür(i)-jen is ečige 'father' + the dative-locative -dür + the reflexive -(i)jen. ülü kelelen is 'not saying' (kele- 'speak' + the converb -n; Ming 說 without 不 given to the verb). 'Without a word' is the sense. The chain continues in the next unit.

sentences.t: bögötür qoṅγor-i unuγ̇ad boro örmüge-ben bögtürüġed Belgütei-lüġe irebe.
sentences.l: Humped sorrel (acc.) having-mounted, blue-grey cloak-his-own having-tied-behind, with-Belgütei, came.
sentences.i: He mounted a humped sorrel horse, tied his own blue-grey cloak behind the saddle, and came with Belgütei.
sentences.n: bögötür (拱脊) is 'humped' and qoṅγor is a yellowish-brown horse colour, Ming 甘草黃, 'liquorice-yellow'; the known-forms glossary has 'bay or dun', and I give 'sorrel' as the nearest English horse colour. boro is Ming 靑 'blue-green / grey'; örmüge is Ming 毛袗, a woollen or felt garment; I call it a cloak. bögtürüġed (捎駄了) is a verb of loading something behind; the stem is uncertain. Belgütei-lüġe is the name + the comitative -lüġe (Ming 一同 'together').

sentences.t: Tere nököčegseġer nököčeküi josun teimü.
sentences.l: That, having-become-companion, companion-being, rule, thus.
sentences.i: That is how he became his companion, and that is the rule of companionship.
sentences.n: Ming 那 自做伴了 做伴的 理 那般. tere is 'that'; nököčegseġer is nököče- 'be a companion' + the participle -gsen + the instrumental -ġer, 'because of having been a companion' (compare iregseġer in §94), with the Ming 自 'of oneself'; nököčeküi is the participle in -küi; josun is 'rule, right way'; teimü closes the sentence, 'so'. The sense is that a companion offers himself without being asked; the Mongol is tightly packed and I have loosened it a little. A moral comment by the narrator.

sentences.t: Seṅgür γoroqan-ača neġüžü Kelüren müren-ü teriġün Burgi ergi-de nutuγlan baγ̇užu
sentences.l: Seṅgür stream-from, having-moved-camp, Kelüren river's head, Burgi bank-at, camping, having-alighted,
sentences.i: They moved camp from the Senggur stream and pitched it on the bank at Burgi, at the head of the Kerülen river,
sentences.n: The place chain: neġüžü 'moving camp', then nutuγlan baγ̇užu 'making a camp, alighting'. nutuγlan is nutuγ 'camping ground' + -la- (to make into) + the converb -n (Ming 營盤做). teriġün is Ming 頭 'head, source'. ergi-de is ergi 'bank, side' with the dative-locative -de. The verb of the sentence, büleġe, is at the next unit boundary; I have divided the chain here and said so.

sentences.t: Sotan eke-jin šidkül keġen qara buluγan daqu abčiražü büleġe.
sentences.l: Sotan the mother's, first-meeting-gift, saying, black sable fur-coat having-brought, had-been.
sentences.i: Sotan, the mother, had brought a black sable coat as her first-meeting gift for the in-laws.
sentences.n: Ming 一見公姑的禮 for šidkül: the present given when a bride first meets her husband's parents ('the rite of first seeing father- and mother-in-law'). eke-jin is 'of the mother' (the genitive -jin after a vowel); the Mongol line does not say what 'the mother's gift' is a gift to, and I read it as Sotan's gift to the bridegroom's household. keġen here makes 'saying' = 'called'. abčiražü is abčira- 'bring along' + -žü. büleġe, 'had been', closes it as a past perfect.

sentences.t: Tere daqu-ji Temüžin, Qasar, Belgütei γurban abču odču

sentences.i: Taking that coat, the three, Temüjin, Qasar and Belgütei, went,
sentences.n: A converb pair, abču odču. γurban, 'three', follows the three names it counts. The commas after Temüžin and Qasar are Shiratori's. The reason for going is told in the quotations that follow: they go to Wang Qan.

sentences.t: "erte üdür Jesügei Qān ečige-lüġe Kereid irgen-ü Waṅ-Qān anda keġeldügsen ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: "Formerly day, Jesügei Qān father-with, Kereid people's Waṅ-Qān sworn-brother, mutually-saying, was.
sentences.i: "In former days Wang Qan of the Kereid people swore brotherhood with my father, Yesügei Qan.
sentences.n: erte üdür is Ming 在前 日子, 'in former days'. anda (契交) is a sworn brother, a blood-brotherhood tie. keġeldügsen is keġe- 'say' + the reciprocal -ldü- + the participle -gsen, 'having spoken to one another', i.e. sworn to one another. Waṅ-Qān is Chinese wang 'prince' with qan; the Ming only says 人名 'a man's name'. Ečige-lüġe 'with father' stands after the name Jesügei Qān (Ming 人名 皇帝 父 一同), so I read it as 'with father Yesügei Qan', Temüjin speaking of his own father; this makes the whole sentence a reading from the Ming and only moderately sure.

morph.gloss: Yesügei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
the Kereid, a people name [種名]
Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (personal name; Chinese wang 'prince' plus qan) [人名]

sentences.t: Ečige-lüġe min-u anda keġeldügsen ečige metü bi že" keġen
sentences.l: Father-with, my sworn-brother mutually-saying, father like am indeed," saying,
sentences.i: He swore brotherhood with my father; he is like a father to me," he said.
sentences.n: Ming 父 一同 我的 契交 相說了 父 般 有 也者. The grammatical person is hard: 'I am like a father' would make no sense, so bi (有) is the verb 'is' with the person understood: 'he is like a father'. min-u is bi 'I' in the genitive stem min- + -u, 'my'. metü (般) is 'like, as'. že (也者) is 'indeed'. keġen (麽道) closes the quotation.

morph.gloss: is, are (verb; possibly a short form of bü-) [有]
converb that closes a quotation: saying

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān-i Tuγ̇ula-jin qara tün-(n)e bijü keġen medežü odba.
sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān (acc.), Tuγ̇ula's black forest-in, is, saying, having-known, went.
sentences.i: Knowing that Wang Qan was in the Black Forest on the Tula, they went.
sentences.n: Ming 河名的 黑 林行 有 麽道 知着 去了. Tuγ̇ula-jin is a river name with the genitive -jin; tün-(n)e is tün 'forest' with the dative-locative -(n)e. bijü (有) is the present of bü- 'be'. keġen medežü, 'saying, knowing', is as in §94. The English 'they' covers Temüjin and his two brothers, the three who set out above; the Mongol does not say 'they'.

sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān-to Temüžin, having-reached, saying:
sentences.i: Temüjin came to Wang Qan and said:
sentences.n: Waṅ-Qān-dur is the name with the dative-locative -dur, Ming 行 'to'. kürčü is kür- 'reach' with the converb -čü (after r). ügülerün opens his speech to the Qan.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (personal name; Chinese wang 'prince' plus qan) [人名行]
converb: having ...-ed, ...-ing (after r or a vowel)

sentences.t: "Erte üdür ečige-lüġe min-u anda keġeldügsen ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: "Formerly day father-with, my sworn-brother mutually-saying, was.
sentences.i: "In former days you swore brotherhood with my father.
sentences.n: The same sentence as in 213-223, shortened and now spoken to Wang Qan. The Mongol has no 'you'; the Ming gives only 'father with, my sworn brother, mutually said, was'. I supply 'you' because he is addressing the Qan.

sentences.t: Ečige kü metü bijü že" keġežü
sentences.l: Father also like, being indeed," having-said,
sentences.i: You are like a father to me," he said, and
sentences.n: Ečige kü metü is 'father also like', kü (只) a particle of emphasis, Ming 只 'just'; bijü is 'is'; že (也者) 'indeed'. keġežü (說着) closes the quotation as a converb, so the sentence runs on to the gift.

sentences.t: gergei baγ̇ulžu emüsgeg čima-da abčiraba" keġen buluγan daqu ögbe.
sentences.l: Wife having-made-descend, first-meeting-gift you-to, I-brought," saying, sable fur-coat gave.
sentences.i: "I have taken a wife, and I have brought you the first-meeting gift," he said, and gave him the sable coat.
sentences.n: baγ̇ulžu (下着) is baγ̇ul-, the causative of baγu- 'descend', plus -žu; Ming 下着 'having lowered'. In context I read 'gave the wife a place' = 'took a wife in', but the idiom is not certain. emüsgeg (上見) is the gift of first meeting, the same custom as šidkül (§96 above), and appears here as a variant name for the coat. čima-da is či 'you' in the stem čima- with the dative -da. The speaker is Temüjin, offering the coat Sotan gave.

sentences.t: "Qara buluγan daqu-jin qariγ̇u qaγačaγsan ulus-i čin-u qamtudqažu ögsü.
sentences.l: "Black sable fur-coat's return, parted people (acc.), you-of, having-gathered, I-will-give.
sentences.i: "In return for the black sable coat, I will gather your scattered people and give them back to you.
sentences.n: qariγ̇u (囘) is 'answer, return (gift)'; daqu-jin is the genitive of 'coat'. qaγačaγsan is qaγača- 'part' + the participle -γsan, 'who have parted'. qamtudqažu is qamtudqa- 'bring together' (from qamtu 'together'), the Ming 相合着. ögsü is ög- 'give' + the optative -sü, 'let me give / I shall give'. Shiratori's full stop closes the promise.

sentences.t: buluγan daqu-jin qariγ̇u butaraγsan ulus-i čin-u bügüdkeldüžu ögsü.
sentences.l: Sable fur-coat's return, scattered people (acc.), you-of, having-made-whole, I-will-give.
sentences.i: In return for the sable coat, I will make your scattered people whole again and give them to you.
sentences.n: The same promise again, with butaraγsan (漫散了的, 'dispersed') for qaγačaγsan and bügüdkeldüžu (完全着 'making complete') for qamtudqažu. The doubling is a form of emphasis, the way the Secret History often pairs two synonyms. bügüdkeldü- is my reading of the stem.

morph.gloss: you (stem čin- before case endings) [你的]
to make complete, make whole (stem inferred from the Ming) [完全着]

sentences.t: Bögöre-jin bögse-dür čegere-jin čeġeži-dür atuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: Kidney's point-in, chest's diaphragm-in, let-it-be," said.
sentences.i: "Keep it in the point of your kidney, in the hollow of your chest," he said.
sentences.n: A proverbial charge, 'keep this in your heart'. Ming 腰子的 尖兒裏 腔子的 胷膈裏 存着, 'in the tip of the kidney, in the diaphragm of the chest, keeping'. bögöre, čegere and bögse are body words I know only from the Ming; atuγai is a- 'be' with an optative-like -tuγai, 'let it stay'. The sense, to carry the promise deep in the body, I take from the Ming, not from the Mongol.

sentences.t: Tendēče qarižu Burgi ergi-de büküi-dür

sentences.n: qarižu is qari- 'turn back' plus -žu, Ming 囘著; the dative-locative ergi-de is as in §96; büküi-dür is 'when being'. A scene-setting clause for the arrival of the old man.

sentences.n: üčügen is 'small'; keġen is the quotation marker; abču odulaγ̇a, 'taking, went' (a converb pair). The sense I take: Jarchiudai gave Jelme to Temüjin as a boy, then took him home again because he was too young. The Mongol is brief, and 'back' is my gloss.

sentences.t: nigen manaγar erte gerel širal üdürge-jin büküi-dür
sentences.l: One clear early light, yellow day-end's, being-when,
sentences.i: when the clear yellow light of early morning was coming,
sentences.n: Obscure. Ming 一 清 早 光 黃 盡將明 有的時: 'one clear early light, yellow, nearly dawn'. nigen manaγar erte is an odd run (the glossary gives manaγar 'tomorrow' or 'early morning'); gerel is 'light' and širal 'yellow'. üdürge-jin (盡將明) I cannot analyse: I take it as the genitive of a word for 'day-break'. The English follows the sense given by the Ming and is not certain.

sentences.t: Höġelün eke-jin ger dotora ködölküi Γoγ̇aγčin emegen bosču ügülerün:
sentences.l: Höġelün mother's, home inside, moving, Γoγ̇aγčin old-woman, having-risen, saying:
sentences.i: Qo'aqchin, the old woman who worked in the mother Hö'elün's tent, rose and said:
sentences.n: ködölküi (動使的) is ködöl- 'move, work' plus the participle -küi, Ming 'one who is set in motion', i.e. a servant; I give 'who worked'. Γoγ̇aγčin is a woman's name (婦人名) and emegen is 'old woman' (老婦人). bosču is bos- 'rise' + -ču. Shiratori prints the first letter of her name with the capital Γ.

morph.gloss: Hö'elün, a woman's name (personal name) [母名]
Qo'aqchin, a woman's name (personal name) [婦人名]
converb: having ...-ed, ...-ing (after r or a vowel)

sentences.t: "Eke eke! Öter bos.
sentences.l: "Mother, mother! quickly rise.
sentences.i: "Mother, mother! Get up quickly.
sentences.n: eke is 'mother' and here a respectful address. öter (疾快) is 'quickly' and bos is the bare stem of bos- 'rise' used as a command.

morph.gloss: to rise (bare stem as a command) [起]

sentences.t: Γažar derbelü- müi; tübüriġün sonostamu;
sentences.l: Earth trembling is; shaking's sound is-heard;
sentences.i: The earth is trembling; I can hear the sound of the shaking;
sentences.n: Ming 地 顫動 有 震的聲 聽得有. Shiratori prints derbelü- with a hyphen and müi separately; I take the pair as derbelü-müi, 'trembles' (derbelü- the stem, -müi a present ending, Ming 有). tübüriġün (震的聲) is a noun 'the sound of shaking'. sonostamu is sonos- 'hear' + -ta- (Ming 得, 'be able') + -mu; the middle suffix is a guess. The semicolons are Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to shake, tremble (stem; written apart from the ending) [顫動]

sentences.t: žalγamsiγtan Taičiγ̇ud aisun aqun-u.
sentences.l: Alarming ones, Taičiγ̇ud, come, perhaps.
sentences.i: It may be the Taichi'ud, who frighten us, coming.
sentences.n: Doubtful. Ming 擾怕了的(每) 姓氏 來 莫不有. žalγamsiγtan I can only analyse as 'those who disturb / frighten' (the Ming 擾怕了 'have disturbed and frightened'); the form is unclear, and the plural (每) may refer to the Taichi'ud. aqun-u (莫不有) is 'is it not so that?', a question-form, 'perhaps'. This is the Taichi'ud of §94, the brothers who envy Temüjin. aisun is as in §93.

morph.gloss: those who frighten or harass (Ming 擾怕了的; form uncertain) [擾怕了的(每)]
the Taichi'ud, a people or clan name [種名]
perhaps, may it not be (Ming 莫不有; analysis uncertain) [莫不有]

sentences.t: Eke öter bos" keġebi.
sentences.l: Mother, quickly rise," said.
sentences.i: Mother, get up quickly," she said.
sentences.n: A repeat of the call, closing with keġebi (說了), keġe- 'say' plus the past -bi, a variant of -ba. The speaker is Qo'aqchin, as the opening of the quotation shows.

morph.gloss: to rise (bare stem as a command) [起]

sentences.t: Höġelün eke ügülerün:
sentences.l: Höġelün the mother, saying:
sentences.i: The mother, Hö'elün, said:
sentences.n: Hö'elün answers by giving orders; the speech is the next unit.

morph.gloss: Hö'elün, a woman's name (personal name) [母名]

sentences.t: "Köġüd-i öter seriġülüdkün" kēġed
sentences.l: "Sons (acc.), quickly, make-awake," having-said,
sentences.i: "Wake the boys quickly," she said, and
sentences.n: köġüd-i is köġün 'son' with the plural -d and the accusative -i. seriġülüdkün is seri- 'wake' + the causative -ġül- + the plural imperative -dkün (Ming 喚敎覺來, 'call and make them wake'); the analysis of the ending is a guess. kēġed, as before, 'having said'.

morph.gloss: to wake, be awake [喚敎覺來]

sentences.t: Höġelün eke öter kü bosbi.
sentences.l: Höġelün the mother quickly also rose.
sentences.i: Mother Hö'elün rose quickly too.
sentences.n: kü (也) is 'also' here. bosbi is bos- 'rise' + the past -bi (Ming 起了). The unit after this one begins with the sons rising.

morph.gloss: Hö'elün, a woman's name (personal name) [母名]

sentences.t: Temüžin-tan köġüd öterlen kü bosuγ̇ad morid(i)-jan barižu
sentences.l: Temüžin-and-the-rest, sons, quickly also having-risen, horses-their-own having-taken,
sentences.i: Temüjin and the other sons rose quickly, and each took his own horse,
sentences.n: Temüžin-tan is the name with -tan (Ming 等 'and the others'), a collective. köġüd is the plural 'sons'. öterlen is öter 'quick' with an adverbial -len. bosuγ̇ad is bos- + the converb -γ̇ad. morid(i)-jan is mori 'horse' + the plural -d + the reflexive -(i)jan, 'their own horses'. barižu is bari- 'take hold of' + -žu. The converb chain stops here; the next unit gives the riding.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form; the bracketed i is Shiratori's)
to take hold of, grasp [拿着]

sentences.t: Temüžin nigen mori unuba.
sentences.l: Temüžin one horse rode.
sentences.i: Temüjin mounted one horse.
sentences.n: The start of the list of who rode what. Each of the following lines has the same shape, 'name, one horse, rode', with nigen mori unuba, until Börte-Üjin's turn: unuba is unu- 'ride' + the past -ba.

sentences.t: Höġelün eke nigen mori unuba. Qasar nigen mori unuba.
sentences.l: Höġelün the mother one horse rode. Qasar one horse rode.
sentences.i: His mother Hö'elün mounted one horse. Qasar mounted one horse.
sentences.n: The same formula for two riders. Shiratori's full stops close each sentence.

morph.gloss: Hö'elün, a woman's name (personal name) [母名]
Qasar, a son's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: Qačiγ̇un nigen mori unuba. Temüge-Ödčigin nigen mori unuba. Belgütei nigen mori unuba.
sentences.l: Qačiγ̇un one horse rode. Temüge-Ödčigin one horse rode. Belgütei one horse rode.
sentences.i: Qachi'un mounted one horse. Temüge-Otchigin mounted one horse. Belgütei mounted one horse.
sentences.n: Three more of the same. The names are Qachi'un and Temüge-Ödchigin (the Ming has (兒)名 'a son's name' for both) and Belgütei.

morph.gloss: Qachi'un, a son's name (personal name) [人名]
Temüge-Ödchigin, a son's name (personal name) [人名]
Belgütei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču nigen mori unuba. Želme nigen mori unuba.
sentences.l: Boγ̇orču one horse rode. Želme one horse rode.
sentences.i: Bo'orchu mounted one horse. Jelme mounted one horse.
sentences.n: The Ming glosses Boγ̇orču here as 女名行 'a woman's name' with the case 行; I cannot account for it, since in §§93-96 he is a man (Ming 人名), and I take it as a glossator's slip for 'a man's name'. Jelme (兒名) is the son of the old man.

morph.gloss: Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [女名 行]
Jelme, a son's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: Temülün-(n)i Höġelün eke ebür-tür(i)-jen deġürbe.
sentences.l: Temülün (acc.), Höġelün the mother, lap-in-her-own, carried.
sentences.i: Hö'elün carried Temülün in her lap.
sentences.n: Temülün is Ming 女名行 'a girl's name' with the accusative (n)i; she is the youngest child, and so rides with her mother. ebür-tür(i)-jen is ebür 'lap, bosom' (懷) + -tür (dative-locative) + the reflexive -(i)jen. deġürbe is deġür- 'carry' + -be.

morph.gloss: Temülün, a girl's name (personal name) [女名 行]
Hö'elün, a woman's name (personal name) [母名]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the bracketed i is Shiratori's)

sentences.t: Nigen mori kötöl žasaba.
sentences.l: One horse spare prepared.
sentences.i: They readied one horse as a spare.
sentences.n: kötöl (從) is a word I take as 'led / following', a horse led alongside; the known-forms gloss is uncertain too. žasaba is žasa- 'prepare' + -ba. The subject is not written, and I have kept it indefinite, 'they'.

morph.gloss: led, following on the lead (sense uncertain) [從馬]
to prepare, set in order [整治了]

sentences.t: Börte-Üžin-e mori dutaba.
sentences.l: Börte-Üžin-for horse lacked.
sentences.i: For Börte-Üjin there was no horse.
sentences.n: dutaba (闕了) is duta- 'be lacking' plus the past -ba. The part ends on a shortage. Börte-Üžin-e is the name with the dative -e, Ming 行. Nothing in the Mongol says why; the English leaves it as a bare fact.

morph.gloss: Börte-Üjin, a woman's name (personal name) [婦人名行]
